card.hook: Most campus photos are taken from the ground, with a lamp post sticking out of someone's head. Go up to the fourth floor of the library and the whole campus lays itself out for you, with the big chapel sitting right in the middle.
card.stand_here: Stand on the fourth-floor balcony of the Christopher Center Library, which you reach by stairs or the elevator from inside. The university lies 147 m to the north-west of the balcony, so face north-west and look for the chapel.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get buildings, lawns and trees in one frame. Then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the chapel. Use 0.5x only if you want lots of sky and ground.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the chapel on an upper crossing point with the trees and lawns filling the bottom, then tap the chapel and slide darker if the sky is washing out.
card.best_time: Go in daylight, because the balcony is open only while the sun is up and the weather allows it. Check the forecast before you climb up.
card.selfie_here: Head down to the Resurrection Labyrinth on the chapel grounds and stand inside it with the chapel behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and let the building fill the background.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand near the Duesenberg Welcome Center drive, where the chapel is in view, so the whole chapel fits in your shot.
card.rules_and_safety: The balcony is inside a university library, so check the official site before you go to confirm current access. Rest your phone on the rail or hold it close to any glass to keep it steady and avoid reflections.
card.challenge: Take one tidy gridlines shot of the chapel, then one wide shot of the whole campus, and see which one you'd actually frame.
card.good_to_know: Valparaiso University is a Lutheran university that began in 1859 and now covers 350 acres. The Chapel of the Resurrection was dedicated in 1959 to replace a worship space lost to fire in 1956. It's one of the largest chapels on a US college campus and stands on the campus's highest point, which is why it's so easy to spot from above.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the fourth-floor balcony of the Christopher Center Library, which you reach by stairs or the elevator from inside. The university lies 147 m to the north-west of the balcony, so face north-west and look for the chapel.

card.hook: You can spot this chapel from U.S. Route 30, so it clearly likes being looked at. It sits on the highest ground on campus, which makes it the easy star of any wide shot.
card.stand_here: Head up to the Christopher Center Library balcony, off the East Quad across from the University Center for the Arts. From the campus it's about 2 minutes on foot, and the chapel is to the north-east, so face that way for a raised view with the campus spread out below.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x from the balcony to fit the chapel and the campus around it. Then try 2x, if your phone has it, to pick out the star-shaped roof and the bell tower. Drop to 0.5x at the labyrinth or inside to fit in the tall windows.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the chapel on one of the vertical lines, and keep the phone level so the tall walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Go in daytime. The balcony is open only while the sun is up and the weather allows. If you want the inside, avoid service times, when photography may be limited.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera at the Resurrection Labyrinth, on the east side of the chapel. Stand inside it or at its edge so the chapel's outside walls are over your shoulder, and try 0.5x to squeeze in more of the building.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by up on the Christopher Center Library balcony, off the East Quad across from the University Center for the Arts, to take your photo with the chapel in the view.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working chapel, so be quick and discreet if a service or rehearsal is under way. The library balcony is open only in daylight and fair weather, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Find the nine-pointed star in the apse roof, then get it in a shot with the bell tower in the same frame.
card.good_to_know: Work on the chapel began in 1956 and it was dedicated in 1959. The chancel is circular and about 30 m high, and the stained glass windows inside are about 29 m tall, designed by Peter Dohmen. The Brandt Campanile, a 44 m bell tower, stands to the south-west of the chapel.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head up to the Christopher Center Library balcony, off the East Quad across from the University Center for the Arts. From the campus it's about 2 minutes on foot, and the chapel is to the north-east, so face that way for a raised view with the campus spread out below.

card.hook: Here's a fun one: a grand limestone courthouse that's missing its tower, and the story of why is the best part of your photo. Come for the tree-lined street view, stay for the caption.
card.stand_here: Stand at the southeast corner of the Lincolnway and Franklin Street intersection, and face west along Lincolnway. The courthouse is to the south-west of you, about 1 minute on foot, and the square's trees run along that side.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the street view along Lincolnway. Switch to 0.5x to squeeze the trees, the street and the building into one frame. For close-ups of the limestone walls, try 2x or higher, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and let the line of the street lead the eye down the picture, and keep your phone level so the walls stay upright.
card.best_time: Soft morning or late-afternoon light flatters pale stone and gives the tree shadows some shape. Midday sun can look a bit flat.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x, and hold the phone slightly higher so you get more of the scene. Keep the courthouse or the tree-lined street over your shoulder, and take a few in case a car or passer-by photobombs.
card.rules_and_safety: Keep to the pavement and watch for traffic as you line up the shot. If you want to go inside the courthouse, check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the courthouse is only half in the frame, then one from inside Courthouse Square where you get the whole building, and see which one you like best.
card.good_to_know: The present courthouse dates from 1883 and is built of Indiana limestone from Ellettsville. It originally had a 168-foot central tower with a clock on each side. A fire on 27 December 1934 gutted it in freezing weather, and the tower was never rebuilt, so what you see today is largely the 1937 restoration.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the southeast corner of the Lincolnway and Franklin Street intersection, and face west along Lincolnway. The courthouse is to the south-west of you, about 1 minute on foot, and the square's trees run along that side.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot or a passer-by spot for the Porter County Courthouse, so I have left these empty rather than guess. The closest material: the Valparaiso city Courthouse Square page (https://www.ci.valparaiso.in.us/266/Courthouse-Square) has photo galleries for the courthouse and for 'Lincolnway and Courthouse Square' but gives no viewpoints. Markfortney's courthouse photo page (https://markfortney.com/valparaiso-courthouse-photos/) shows south and west views of the building but does not name where they were taken. The rest were historic postcards and archive photos (Flickr, Wikimedia Commons, Indiana Memory) with no visitor-photo guidance. No selfie-stick, tripod, or safety rules appeared on any page. A local photo guide or a map check of the Courthouse Square corners would be needed to fill this in.

card.hook: Most town squares feel like a postcard. This one feels like a Tuesday, with shops open, people heading to work and old limestone buildings carrying on around them. That's the fun of it.
card.stand_here: Stand in Central Park Plaza, about 150 m west of the centre of the district, out on the open lawn or along the walkways. Turn to face the downtown buildings, with the centre of the district to the east.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to take in the whole plaza and the buildings around it. Switch to 1x for a natural look at the storefronts, then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out courthouse and bank details from where you stand.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines to keep the building edges straight, and tap the buildings so the stone looks right. If the sky is bright, slide it a little darker to keep the colours.
card.best_time: Morning or late afternoon gives softer light on the building fronts. The plaza is often quieter earlier in the day, so you'll get more space to step back.
card.selfie_here: Walk the paths across the grass in Central Park Plaza, with the Orville Redenbacher statue nearby. Use the front camera at 0.5x and the downtown buildings ringing the plaza will fill the background behind you.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by in Courthouse Square to take it while you stand with the Porter County Courthouse behind you and they face it from across the square.
card.rules_and_safety: Central Park Plaza is an open public park. Events can change how the plaza is set up, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Find the arched bank windows and stone pillars, then take one close-up of each. Bonus points if the Orville Redenbacher statue gets a smile in a shot too.
card.good_to_know: The Porter County Courthouse dates from 1885. It was restored after a fire in 1934 destroyed its distinctive clock tower. The town started as Portersville in 1836 and was renamed the next year, after Commodore David Porter's last battle off the Chilean port of Valparaíso.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Central Park Plaza, about 150 m west of the centre of the district, out on the open lawn or along the walkways. Turn to face the downtown buildings, with the centre of the district to the east.

card.hook: Here's the twist: the best photo at the Christopher Center isn't of the library at all. You head inside, go up to the fourth floor, and shoot the view of the Chapel and the campus from the balcony.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the fourth-floor balcony inside the Christopher Center. Find the library first, go in, take the stairs or the elevator up, and face out over the Chapel and the campus.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to catch the whole sweep of campus. Then try 1x for a natural view, and zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Chapel.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, put the Chapel on one of the lines and keep the horizon level, then tap the Chapel and slide darker a touch if the sky looks washed out.
card.best_time: Go in daylight so the campus view is nicely lit. Check the campus map for current access before you set off.
card.selfie_here: Flip to the front camera, try zoom 0.5x if your phone offers it, and hold your arm out so the view sits behind your shoulder. Take a couple of frames so you can pick the one where you're not squinting.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a university library, so access and hours may change. Check the campus map or the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Take the same view at 0.5x, 1x and 2x, then pick a winner and see if you chose the wide one or the close one.
card.good_to_know: The Christopher Center opened as Valparaiso University's fourth library. It replaced the older Moellering Library, which was demolished in 2005. The Chicago firm Esherick Homsey Dodge & Davis designed it, and the grid-like structure along the south and east sides gives it its look and works as a sunscreen.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the fourth-floor balcony inside the Christopher Center. Find the library first, go in, take the stairs or the elevator up, and face out over the Chapel and the campus.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a spot where a visitor has the Christopher Center (Valparaiso University's library, 1410 Chapel Drive) behind them, so I returned no selfie spots. The only Christopher Center photo spot I found is the fourth-floor balcony, which a campus-tour blog recommends for its view of the Chapel of the Resurrection, so the library is the viewpoint rather than the backdrop. Source: 'TOP SPOTS TO TAKE A PHOTO ON YOUR CAMPUS TOUR - Valparaiso University', https://www.valpo.edu/top-spots-to-take-a-photo-on-your-campus-tour/. The Wikipedia coordinates for the library (41.462705, -87.043139) match the given position, so the place is the right one. No page I found names a spot where a passer-by should stand to photograph a visitor with the whole library in frame, and no page states selfie stick or tripod rules or a safety point. The Wikipedia article mentions Resurrection Meadow south of the chapel, which the library's reading room overlooks, but no page recommends it as a photo position. Searches were limited, so a different photo guide could still cover a backdrop spot.
